title: Deployment economics scenarios snapshot
summary: Compact snapshot of scenario-level economics comparing three private deployment approaches (on-prem owned, colo/hybrid, managed VPC reserved capacity) plus a micro-model for license+support bundle packaging. Includes baseline assumptions, line-item cost breakup, amortization and breakeven outputs, and pragmatic recommendations for packaging and pricing levers.
scope: Focus: 3-year financial view for customers of mid-market size (10-50 inference GPUs equivalent). Purpose: give GTM and solutions engineering a quick reference for proposal math and negotiation levers. Not a full audit; numbers are sample-level and parameterized for the referenced spreadsheet.
assumptions: Target workload: 200M tokens/day (mixed short/long chat), 9.5M tokens/hour peak window
Equivalent GPU capacity: estimate 12 A100-40GB equivalents (see spreadsheet for mapping to model/quantization)
On-prem hardware list price per A100-equivalent node: $70k (includes 2xNVMe, 512GB RAM, rack+network amortized), refresh cycle 4 years
Managed VPC: reserved pool pricing yields ~35% discount vs on-demand hosted for committed 12-mo capacity
License fees: base platform license is annual, tiers: Starter $50k/yr, Professional $150k/yr, Enterprise $350k/yr
Support bundles: Silver (8x5) 10% of license, Gold (24x7) 20% of license + optional SRE retainer $8k/mo, Platinum 30% + SLA credits
Network egress: assumed 0.2TB/day of payloads at $0.08/GB for cloud-hosted egress; on-prem egress considered internal
Discounting: NPV not used; simple payback / breakeven year and 3-year total cost of ownership used for quick comparisons
cost_line_items: Capital: hardware, rack PDUs, initial install labor (hours * $150/hr)
Recurring infra OPEX: colo rent, power, maintenance contracts, spare parts reserve
Cloud managed fees: reserved capacity charges, ingress/egress, control plane ops fee
Software: annual platform license, optional per-seat admin fees
Support: percent-of-license bundles, optional SRE retainer, professional services for onboarding
People ops: internal infra ops FTE fraction (percent of 1-2 SREs), training
scenario_baselines: Scenario A - On-prem owned: Buy 12 nodes up front (capex ~ $840k), install, run in customer DC. 3-year TCO = capex + 36 months OPEX (power, maintenance $10k/mo) + license + support.
Scenario B - Colocation hybrid: Buy 8 nodes, place in colo, burst to managed VPC for peak. Combo of capex (8 nodes ~$560k) + colo fees + reserved hosted bursts. Good when DC ops limited.

Scenario C - Managed VPC reserved pool: No capex. Annual committed contract to Redwood Dedicated reserved pool sized to sustained demand (equivalent cost ~ $380k/yr with 35% reserved discount vs on-demand). 3-year TCO = 3 * committed fee + license + support
sample_outputs: 3-year TCO (sample): On-prem: $1.05M (capex $840k + licenses/support $120k + ops $90k), Colocation hybrid: $0.92M, Managed VPC reserved: $1.14M
Simple payback (on-prem): breakeven vs managed VPC at ~2.1 years given sample ops/labor assumptions
Unit cost per 1M tokens (3y average): On-prem $0.68, Colocation hybrid $0.60, Managed VPC reserved $0.76
Sensitivity: +20% hardware price shift changes on-prem 3y TCO by ~+$168k; +20% colo rates moves hybrid by +$40k per year
pricing_and_bundle_recs: Offer a bundled Professional license + Gold support at a 12% bundled discount for customers committing 12 months of dedicated/reserved capacity. Rationale: reduces sticker shock vs separate line items and smooths renewals
Introduce a 'Hardware Buyback' option for on-prem customers at contract year 2 to lower net capex by up to 15% — attractive for SMBs with uncertain growth
Create a tiered SRE retainer (Bronze $3k/mo, Silver $8k/mo, Gold $15k/mo) to upsell customers who select Silver/Gold support and require hands-on ops
For customers with bursty traffic, recommend hybrid colo + managed-burst product with clear chargebacks for burst usage and a per-Mi token incremental rate to avoid open-ended costs
Price anchoring: show customers a 3-line quote (capex-only, capex+support, managed-commit) to highlight tradeoffs and support negotiation
negotiation_levers: Shorten license term to 12 months for larger up-front discounts but tie discount depth to committed pool size
Trade off: higher support % for lower license base if customer wants predictable OPEX
Offer milestone-based professional services credits (e.g., first-month onboarding waived) to reduce initial cash barrier
Allow one-time capacity add-on credits in year 1 at pre-negotiated rates to avoid mid-contract repricing disputes
risks_and_open_questions: Customer DC network constraints and cross-site latency assumptions need validation — affects hybrid model economics
Hardware lead times (12-20 weeks) can push deployment out and change cashflow for on-prem buys
Software license consumption model (per-node vs per-throughput) must be clarified for accurate per-token math
Audit of customer's internal FTE costs required for accurate SRE/Ops offset — we currently use industry averages
